# domainchief_dns_record (Resource)

Manages a DNS record of a domain that uses Domain Chief hosted DNS.

Requires a token with the `domainchief:dns:write` scope.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "domainchief_dns_record" "www" {
  domain  = "example.com"
  type    = "CNAME"
  name    = "www"
  content = "example.com"
}

resource "domainchief_dns_record" "mx" {
  domain   = "example.com"
  type     = "MX"
  content  = "mail.example.net"
  priority = 10
  ttl      = 3600
}

resource "domainchief_dns_record" "spf" {
  domain  = "example.com"
  type    = "TXT"
  content = "v=spf1 include:example.net -all"
  comment = "Managed by Terraform"

  metadata = {
    owner = "platform"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `content` (String) The record content. TXT content can be written with or without surrounding quotes, and hostnames with or without a trailing dot.
- `domain` (String) The domain name or domain ID the record belongs to. Changing this creates a new record.
- `type` (String) The record type, one of `A`, `AAAA`, `CNAME`, `MX`, `TXT`, `ALIAS`, `CAA`, `SRV`, `TLSA`, `NS`.

### Optional

- `comment` (String) An optional comment for the record.
- `metadata` (Map of String) Metadata to attach to the record. Keys are at most 40 characters and cannot contain `[` or `]`, values are at most 500 characters. Keys starting with `domainchief:` are reserved for Domain Chief: they cannot be set and the ones Domain Chief adds are not tracked.
- `name` (String) The record name relative to the domain, for example `www`. Use an empty string or `@` for the domain itself. Defaults to the domain itself.
- `priority` (Number) The record priority, only for `MX` and `SRV` records. Other record types always have a priority of `0`. Defaults to `0`.
- `ttl` (Number) The record TTL in seconds, one of `60`, `300`, `900`, `1800`, `3600`, `21600`, `43200`, `86400`, `172800`, `259200`, `604800`, `1209600`, `2592000`. Defaults to `3600`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of the DNS record.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# DNS records are imported using the domain and the record ID.
terraform import domainchief_dns_record.www example.com/01HXYZ0000000000000000000
```
